nodes.description: In Tapt1 knockout mice TAPT1 in the ER binds the surfactant lipid transporter ABCA3. Without TAPT1, ABCA3 is sent for autophagy-lysosomal degradation, lamellar bodies and surfactant are deficient, and pups die of atelectasis-induced respiratory distress. Whether this contributes to the lung anomalies in affected human fetuses is unknown.

evidence.reference_title: Tapt1 deficiency in mice impairs pulmonary lipid homeostasis and normal postnatal respiration by targeting ABCA3 for autophagy-lysosomal degradation.
evidence.snippet: We further reveal that TAPT1 interacts with the ATP-binding cassette transporter A3 (ABCA3), thereby regulating autophagy-lysosomal degradation of ABCA3.

evidence.reference_title: Tapt1 deficiency in mice impairs pulmonary lipid homeostasis and normal postnatal respiration by targeting ABCA3 for autophagy-lysosomal degradation.
evidence.snippet: ABCA3 insufficiency reduces surfactant lipids, leading to defective lamellar body formation and surfactant production.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic Defects in TAPT1 Disrupt Ciliogenesis and Cause a Complex Lethal Osteochondrodysplasia.
evidence.snippet: Knockdown of tapt1b in zebrafish induces severe craniofacial cartilage malformations and delayed ossification, which is shown to be associated with aberrant differentiation of cranial neural crest cells.

nodes.description: In cell lines TAPT1 restrains BMP signaling by bringing SMAD1/5 to the SMURF1 ubiquitin ligase for proteasomal degradation. Two lethal osteochondrodysplasia alleles increased this activity on SMAD1, which would lower BMP output in bone-forming cells. This conflicts with the partial loss-of-function reading of the same alleles and has not been tested in patient tissue.

evidence.reference_title: Transmembrane anterior posterior transformation 1 regulates BMP signaling and modulates the protein stability of SMAD1/5.
evidence.snippet: Herein, we report that TAPT1 inhibits BMP signaling and destabilizes the SMAD1/5 protein by facilitating its interaction with SMURF1 E3 ubiquitin ligase, which leads to SMAD1/5 proteasomal degradation.

evidence.reference_title: Transmembrane anterior posterior transformation 1 regulates BMP signaling and modulates the protein stability of SMAD1/5.
evidence.snippet: Our results also suggested that two lethal osteochondrodysplasia-associated mutations of TAPT1 likely function as gain-of-function (GOF) variants to promote SMAD1 proteasomal degradation.

nodes.description: The original families carried a homozygous missense variant, p.Asp353Val, and a homozygous splice variant causing in-frame skipping of exon 10. Both are thought to leave partial TAPT1 function, in contrast with the protein-null allele that causes osteogenesis imperfecta with neonatal progeroid features and survival into childhood.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic Defects in TAPT1 Disrupt Ciliogenesis and Cause a Complex Lethal Osteochondrodysplasia.
evidence.snippet: Our study demonstrates that TAPT1 mutations underlie a complex congenital syndrome, showing clinical overlap between lethal skeletal dysplasias and ciliopathies.

evidence.reference_title: A progeroid syndrome caused by a deep intronic variant in TAPT1 is revealed by RNA/SI-NET sequencing.
evidence.snippet: Our six new patients carry a complete loss‐of‐function mutation resulting in a protein‐null allele, whereas both prior studies showed partial loss‐of‐function mutations including missense and in‐frame exon 6 and exon 10 skipping (Symoens et al, 2015; Patel et al, 2017).

nodes.description: Congenital brain anomalies; the published abstract does not specify which.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic Defects in TAPT1 Disrupt Ciliogenesis and Cause a Complex Lethal Osteochondrodysplasia.
evidence.snippet: This syndrome is characterized by fetal lethality, severe hypomineralization of the entire skeleton and intra-uterine fractures, and multiple congenital developmental anomalies affecting the brain, lungs, and kidneys.

nodes.description: Patient fibroblasts form fewer normal primary cilia. This places the disorder near the ciliopathies, but fibroblasts from a surviving patient with TAPT1-related osteogenesis imperfecta formed cilia normally, so the weight of the ciliary defect in the skeletal phenotype is uncertain.

evidence.reference_title: Genetic Defects in TAPT1 Disrupt Ciliogenesis and Cause a Complex Lethal Osteochondrodysplasia.
evidence.snippet: We establish that wild-type TAPT1 localizes to the centrosome and/or ciliary basal body, whereas defective TAPT1 mislocalizes to the cytoplasm and disrupts Golgi morphology and trafficking and normal primary cilium formation.

evidence.reference_title: TAPT1-at the crossroads of extracellular matrix and signaling in Osteogenesis imperfecta.
evidence.snippet: We could detect some anomalies in Golgi morphology (Appendix Fig S2) but no defects in ciliogenesis (Appendix Fig S3A–E) that were previously linked to TAPT1 mutations (Symoens et al, 2015).

nodes.description: The whole fetal skeleton is severely undermineralized and fractures occur before birth. Defective collagen secretion and impaired osteogenic differentiation are the proposed causes; their relative contribution is unknown.

nodes.description: In mouse brain and cultured cells TAPT1 sits in the endoplasmic reticulum and binds SUCO. The complex keeps newly synthesized proteins from being treated as misfolded and degraded by ER-associated degradation. Without it, protein degradation is overactive and ER-to-Golgi transport slows. Biallelic SUCO variants also cause a skeletal dysplasia. This node is drawn from knockout mice and cells, not patient tissue.

evidence.reference_title: TAPT1 interacts with SUCO to maintain the homeostasis of newly synthesized proteins and brain development in mice.
evidence.snippet: Mechanically, we reveal that TAPT1 interacts with SUCO in the endoplasmic reticulum to maintain newly synthesized proteins, including those important for brain development.

nodes.description: Wild-type TAPT1 was found at the centrosome and ciliary basal body in fibroblasts, and the disease alleles redistributed it to the cytoplasm. Later fractionation found it in a combined mitochondria/ER/Golgi fraction and mouse studies place it in the endoplasmic reticulum, so where the protein normally acts is not settled.

nodes.description: Perinatal-lethal ENU mutant with posterior-to-anterior homeotic transformations of the mid vertebral column, which led to the gene's name.
Brain-restricted Tapt1 loss gives microcephaly, motor dysfunction and early death through loss of TAPT1-SUCO protein protection in the ER.
Germline Tapt1 deletion causes neonatal death from atelectasis and respiratory distress through loss of ABCA3 and surfactant.
Craniofacial cartilage malformation and delayed ossification.
